newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: CENTRAL BANK DRAWS UP NEW LAW ON ITS ACTIVITY.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL BANK DRAWS UP NEW LAW ON ITS ACTIVITY.

text.p: The Lithuanian central bank said on Thursday that it was in the process of drawing up a new draft law on its activities to meet EU regulations and restrict political influence on the bank.

"In this draft law we will take into account the regulations and requirements of the European Union to maintain the independence of the central bank ," Gitanas Nauseda, the head of the central bank's policy department, told Reuters.
"One of the main objectives of the draft law is that the central bank will not be able to extend credit to the executive branch of government in any form," he said..
"The draft law is in its last phase of preparation," Nauseda added.
He also said that the board of the Bank of Lithuania is expected to consider the draft law in the nearest future.
Political influence on the central bank's policies is currently limited by the country's currency board arrangement, which deprives the central bank of traditional monetary polict instruments.
Under the arrangement, the central bank guarantees that it will have one dollar in circulation for every four litas in circulation, freezing the exchange rate at that level.
The Bank of Lithuania plans to gradually scrap the system over the next two to three years, a move which some analysts say could erode its independence from political influence.
